title: Precision cost & latency synthesizer for per-route/model/customer metrics
creator: Avery Chen
description:
We need a robust backend service that computes high-fidelity cost and latency breakdowns attributed to route, model variant, and customer. This service ("synthesizer") should combine streaming event data, deployment topology metadata, and kernel/hardware cost models to produce both near-real-time per-request attributions and daily rollups for Console and billing reports.

Goals:
- Produce transparent, explainable breakdowns that map tokens and compute to dollar and latency units across route->model->customer dimensions.
- Support both online (minutes) and batch (daily) pipelines with identical decomposition logic.
- Keep cardinality controllable for high-cardinality routes while preserving accuracy for top customers.
- Provide an API endpoint used by Console dashboards, cost alerting, and internal chargeback flows.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route and per-model cost and latency breakdown available in Console for last 7 days
Attribution math reproduces sample billing table within 3% for representative workloads
Query API returns aggregated breakdowns for a single customer in <200ms for 7-day window
Online pipeline provides <2 minute freshness for routes marked 'real-time'
Backfill can regenerate 30 days of rollups within 6 hours for a single region
Caching/aggregation knobs exist to limit cardinality explosion (top-K + other bucket)
Schema and provenance metadata included for every rollup row (model_version, route_id, batch_size, cache_hit_rate)
implementation_plan: Design unified attribution model: tokenize cost drivers (decode/encode tokens, KV cache hits, compute time, GPU-second cost, network egress) and define weightings/priors
Schema: ledger_row with flat fields (date, region, customer_id, route_id, model_hash, tokens_generated, tokens_input, compute_ms, gpu_seconds_est, cost_usd, latency_ms_p50,p95)
Streaming path: consume request/response traces + kernel telemetry via Kafka, enrich with model profile table, run per-request attribution lambda, persist to event_rollup topic
Batch path: nightly Spark job that re-aggregates raw events and reconciles streaming aggregates, emits canonical day partitions in Parquet for long-term reporting
Realtime API: materialize hot windows in Redis/Materialize for Console queries (7d, 24h), fallback to precomputed parquet slices for older ranges
Backfill tooling: parquet-based deterministic replayer that can run on EMR and tag rows with provenance for audit
Accuracy verification: cross-check against billing-raw export; run injection tests with synthetic request traces and golden expected cost table
Observability: SLOs for pipeline lag, per-partition throughput, reconciliation drift; dashboards in Grafana; alerting for >5% drift vs billing
tradeoffs_and_notes: Online attribution is more resource intensive: we will only enable per-request decomposition for routes marked as 'high-fidelity' to control costs
Exact allocation of shared infra (e.g., multi-tenant GPU utilization) will be approximated using time-based pro rata splits; we keep the model pluggable for future improvements
We prioritize explainability over micro-cent precision. The target is reproducible and auditable math rather than perfect cent-level accuracy
High-cardinality customers will be handled with top-K routing dimension and an 'other' bucket to keep storage/query cost predictable
risks: Cardinality blowup for customers with thousands of routes could increase storage and query costs
Mismatch between kernel-level telemetry and billing meter can cause reconciliation drift
Schema changes in model profiles (quantization flags, kernel variants) could require frequent migration re-runs
comments: 2025-02-14 - Avery Chen: Kickoff with product and console PMs. Agreed on two-tier freshness model (near-real-time for critical routes, daily for all others). PM wants per-route slices surfaced in Console cost breakdown panel.
2025-02-20 - Marcus Patel: Completed initial attribution math doc. Chose to attribute network egress at request-level rather than model-level to improve customer-facing explainability.
2025-02-27 - Design review (Ellen Morales): UX needs 'explain allocation' modal that shows how shared infra is split. Added to Console ticket for front-end work.
2025-03-03 - Eng sync: Implemented streaming consumer + enrichment prototype. End-to-end latency for a small sample is ~1.6s. Need to optimize enrichment cache hit rate. See PR #78 for code.

2025-03-05 - Perf test: Running a 24h synthetic replay at peak traffic; observed 12% drift vs nightly billing for first pass. Root cause: kernel telemetry under-reports KV cache hits; working with runtime team to instrument KV hit counts in telemetry (ENG-42002).

2025-03-06 - Marcus Patel: Switched materialization strategy to Redis-based hot windows to improve Console query latency; planning gradual rollout to avoid thundering herd. Follow-up: add rate limiter and circuit-breaker for Console queries.
